userStories.title: Breadcrumb leaf on every project page, 44 px breadcrumb links on narrow screens
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the six missing project breadcrumb leaves and enlarge breadcrumb link touch targets below sm.

**Motivation** — R2-10: `/<project>/approvals`, `/<project>/approval-policies`, `/<project>/timeline`, `/<project>/memory`, `/<project>/code-intel` and `/<project>/settings` fall through `breadcrumbItems` in `layouts/default.vue` to `[Koda, <project>]`, so the bar reads "Koda / sandbox" with the project as the unlinked leaf.

**Approach** — Touch-target convention (from slice 10, R1-20, `pages/[project]/index.vue` priority chips `h-11 sm:h-9`): a control is 44 px (`h-11` / `min-h-11`) below the `sm` breakpoint and keeps its compact size from `sm` up.

Read-only (verified, unchanged):
- `tests/layouts/flows-nav.spec.ts` `breadcrumbItemsFor(path, params)` runs the real `layouts/default.vue` setup for one route and returns `breadcrumbItems.value`; the new breadcrumb spec copies this harness.
- `components/approvals/ProjectApprovalNavLinks.vue` labels its links `t('nav.approvals')` and `t('nav.approvalPolicies')`; the layout sidebar labels the others `t('nav.timeline')`, `t('nav.memory')`, `t('nav.codeIntel')` and `t('nav.settings')`. All six keys exist in both locale files.

Changed. The baseline exists only to locate the code; implement the target.

- `layouts/default.vue` `breadcrumbItems`
  - Baseline: no branch for the six paths; they reach the final `return [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: project }]`.
  - Target: for each path `/${project}/<page>` in the table below, return
    `[{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: project, to: '/' + project }, { label: t(<key>) }]`.

    | page | key |
    |:--|:--|
    | `approvals` | `nav.approvals` |
    | `approval-policies` | `nav.approvalPolicies` |
    | `timeline` | `nav.timeline` |
    | `memory` | `nav.memory` |
    | `code-intel` | `nav.codeIntel` |
    | `settings` | `nav.settings` |

- `components/AppBreadcrumb.vue` link
  - Baseline: `<NuxtLink ... class="hover:text-foreground transition-colors">`
  - Target: the link class adds `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center sm:min-h-0`.

**Scope** — In: the six exact project paths, their linked project ancestor, shared breadcrumb link classes, and the two new behavioral specs, including the existing non-link behavior for items without a destination. Out: US-002 button/reason styling, US-003 filter sizing and US-004 other mobile controls. Breadcrumbs for global pages (no project in the route) are unchanged: the bar stays hidden there. Touch targets beyond the five R2-16 controls are not swept here. Measured touch-target sizes and contrast are checked in the post-merge live sweep on koda-wk, not in unit tests (jsdom has no layout).

**Interface** — Preserve the existing breadcrumb item shape `{ label: string; to?: string }`; the target computed array is `[{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: project, to: '/' + project }, { label: t(<key>) }]`. No new public props or translations.

**Testing** — Use tdd-simple: create `tests/layouts/default-breadcrumb-leaves.spec.ts` by copying the real-setup harness in flows-nav.spec.ts and create `tests/components/app-breadcrumb.spec.ts` with an attribute-forwarding NuxtLink stub. Exercise the real layout setup and component output, keep flows and project-root regressions, and leave sidebar ordering and existing navigation permissions unchanged. No new request or error path.
acceptanceCriteria: When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/timeline with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.timeline' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/memory with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.memory' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/code-intel with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.codeIntel' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/settings with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.settings' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/approvals with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.approvals' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs for path /web/approval-policies with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, breadcrumbItems equals [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.approvalPolicies' }].

When layouts/default.vue setup runs with params { project: 'web' } and an i18n stub returning the key, route /web/flows still gives [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web', to: '/web' }, { label: 'nav.flows' }], and route /web still gives [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web' }], preserving this regression guard.

When AppBreadcrumb renders items [{ label: 'Koda', to: '/' }, { label: 'web' }], its rendered output has a Koda link with classes inline-flex, min-h-11, items-center and sm:min-h-0, and web as a non-link span.

routing.reasoning: Two existing UI files plus focused tests; exact path-to-label additions and responsive link classes use established patterns without changing navigation permissions.

userStories.title: Disabled filled buttons look disabled, the reason sits under the button
userStories.description: **Goal** — Give disabled filled buttons muted styling and place each thread action's accessible reason directly underneath its button. **Motivation** — R2-12: `components/ui/button/Button.vue` styles every disabled variant with `disabled:opacity-50`. On the `default` variant the indigo fill stays, so the KB Search button and the thread Publish/Plan/Run buttons look enabled. In `components/fleet/threads/ThreadActionBar.vue` the reason `` is a sibling of the button in one wrapping row. **Approach** — Read-only (verified, unchanged): - `lib/utils.ts` `cn(...inputs)` = `twMerge(clsx(inputs))`; a later conflicting class wins. Changed. The baseline exists only to locate the code; implement the target. - `components/ui/button/Button.vue` `buttonVariants` - Baseline: `default: 'bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90'`, `destructive: 'bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bg-destructive/90'`, base `disabled:opacity-50`. - Target: the `default` and `destructive` variants add `disabled:bg-muted disabled:text-muted-foreground disabled:opacity-100`. The base and the other variants keep `disabled:opacity-50`. - `components/fleet/threads/ThreadActionBar.vue` action markup - Baseline: `
acceptanceCriteria: When Button renders with variant default and disabled true, the rendered button class includes disabled:bg-muted, disabled:text-muted-foreground and disabled:opacity-100 and does not include disabled:opacity-50.
When Button renders with variant destructive and disabled true, the rendered button class includes disabled:bg-muted, disabled:text-muted-foreground and disabled:opacity-100.
When Button renders with variant outline and disabled true, the rendered button class includes disabled:opacity-50 and does not include disabled:bg-muted.

Given a thread whose writtenPaths is empty, when ThreadActionBar mounts with Publish blocked, thread-action-publish-reason renders as a p with classes text-xs and text-muted-foreground, inside the same flex-col wrapper as thread-action-publish and placed after that button.

Given that blocked-Publish mount, when ThreadActionBar renders, the thread-action-publish button's aria-describedby equals thread-action-publish-reason, matching the reason element's id thread-action-publish-reason.
Given an ask-mode thread with no written path (Publish enabled, no reason), when ThreadActionBar mounts, the thread-action-publish button has no aria-describedby attribute.

routing.reasoning: Two existing components with shared class-merging effects and small semantic markup changes; availability and authorization behavior remain unchanged.

userStories.title: Filter selects as tall as inputs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Share the native filter-control classes so the listed selects and memory search match Input's 40 px height.

**Motivation** — R2-13: the timeline and memory filter selects use `px-2 py-1` (about 29 px), the outbox status select the same, and `components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue` (audit filters) uses `h-9`, while `Input` is `h-10`.

**Approach** — Read-only (verified, unchanged):
- `components/ui/input/Input.vue` renders `h-10`.

Changed. The baseline exists only to locate the code; implement the target.

- `lib/form-control.ts` (new) exports `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS = 'h-10 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm'`, the class for raw native filter controls, matching `Input`'s height.
- `components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue` select class
  - Baseline: `h-9 w-full rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm`
  - Target: `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS` plus `w-full`. Every `FleetNativeSelect` consumer (13 files, including the create-ticket, add-repo, budget, schedule and thread-handoff dialogs, fleet dispatch, new thread and the analytics and log filters) grows from 36 px to 40 px; that is intended, so form selects match `Input` too.
- `pages/[project]/timeline.vue` `#timeline-event-type`, `pages/[project]/memory.vue` `#memory-kind-filter` and `#memory-status-filter`, `pages/admin/outbox.vue` `#outbox-status`
  - Baseline: `rounded-md border border-border bg-background px-2 py-1 text-sm` (outbox adds `w-fit`).
  - Target: `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS` (outbox keeps `w-fit`). They stay native `<select>` elements with their
    current ids, bindings and `@change` handlers.
- `pages/[project]/memory.vue` text search `<input type="search">` in the same filter row
  - Baseline: `rounded-md border border-border bg-background px-2 py-1 text-sm`
  - Target: `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS`; it stays a raw `input` with its `v-model`, `maxlength` and placeholder.

**Scope** — In: the new constant and its same-story consumers NativeSelect.vue, timeline.vue, memory.vue and outbox.vue, including the intentional height change for every FleetNativeSelect consumer; the two new test suites; the narrowly updated obsolete NativeSelect import restriction; and regression coverage preserving native change/blur behavior, including the existing empty-string fallback for a missing change-event target. Out: US-001 breadcrumbs, US-002 button/reason styling and US-004 touch-target markup. Raw `<select>` elements outside the four filter selects (members panel, invites panel, role and principal-role dialogs, approval policy dialog, agents table, backend picker, repo rule override) keep their current classes; `FleetNativeSelect` consumers do change, see Design. Input.vue is read-only. Do not change permission checks, filter logic or select/input types. Measured touch-target sizes and contrast are checked in the post-merge live sweep on koda-wk, not in unit tests (jsdom has no layout).

**Interface** —
```typescript
export const FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS = 'h-10 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm'
```

**Seam** — `FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS` (new export of `lib/form-control.ts`) is consumed in the same story by `NativeSelect.vue`, `timeline.vue`, `memory.vue` and `outbox.vue`; the page-level ACs below render each consumer and assert the rendered select carries `h-10`, which proves the wiring.

**Testing** — Use tdd-simple. Create tests/lib/form-control.spec.ts for the exact export and real NativeSelect classes, and tests/pages/filter-select-height.spec.ts for real page mounts. Reuse memory-readable.spec.ts mountMemory with applyFilters a jest.fn(), outbox harnesses in admin-outbox*.spec.ts, and timeline's existing coverage plus mount-sfc with the required Nuxt globals. The current timeline.spec.ts has no exported mount helper, so construct its actual page mount using the shared renderer. Invoke memory-kind-filter's onChange once and expect one applyFilters call; preserve the existing ids/bindings/handlers. IMPORTANT repository discrepancy: tests/components/fleet-native-select.spec.ts currently contains an imports-only-Vue source restriction at lines 63-66. Narrowly update that obsolete test to allow the required shared constant import, retaining all existing value/change/blur/id/placeholder assertions; this corrects the spec's inaccurate claim that no existing test modification is needed. No new request or error path.
acceptanceCriteria: When FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS is imported from lib/form-control, its value is the string h-10 rounded-md border border-input bg-background px-3 text-sm.
When FleetNativeSelect (components/fleet/NativeSelect.vue) renders with two options, the rendered select class includes h-10 and w-full and does not include h-9.
When pages/[project]/timeline.vue mounts, the #timeline-event-type select class includes h-10 and border-input.
When pages/[project]/memory.vue mounts, both #memory-kind-filter and #memory-status-filter render with classes including h-10.
When pages/admin/outbox.vue mounts, the #outbox-status select class includes h-10 and w-fit.
When pages/[project]/memory.vue mounts, the text search input (type search) class includes h-10 and border-input.

Given the memory page with useMemory stubbed as in tests/pages/memory-readable.spec.ts mountMemory but applyFilters a jest.fn(), when the #memory-kind-filter select's onChange prop is called, applyFilters is called once, preserving this regression guard that passes before and after the change.

Given a rendered FleetNativeSelect, when its native change handler receives an event with target null, it emits update:modelValue with the empty string, preserving the existing missing-target fallback.

routing.reasoning: One static class constant and four existing consumers form a small same-story seam; broad NativeSelect propagation is intentional, with no new abstraction beyond the constant or behavioral filter changes.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test `the SFC imports nothing but vue (the mount helper only provides vue)` asserts NativeSelect.vue has no import other than `vue`; NativeSelect now imports FILTER_CONTROL_CLASS from the new lib form-control module (tilde alias), and mountSfc resolves tilde-alias imports to real files, so the test now allows exactly vue and that one module and still rejects any other import (rename it to say so).

userStories.title: 44 px touch targets for the small controls on narrow screens
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enlarge the specified audit, approval-notification, notification-preference and flow state controls on narrow screens while retaining compact desktop sizes.

**Motivation** — R2-16: at 390 px the breadcrumb links are 20 px tall, the audit row expand button 20x20, the notification-settings checkboxes 16x16, the approval-notification toggle 32 px, and the flow list state links 17 px.

**Approach** — Touch-target convention (from slice 10, R1-20, `pages/[project]/index.vue` priority chips `h-11 sm:h-9`): a control is 44 px (`h-11` / `min-h-11`) below the `sm` breakpoint and keeps its compact size from `sm` up.

Changed. The baseline exists only to locate the code; implement the target.

- `pages/admin/audit.vue` `data-testid="audit-expand"` button
  - Baseline: `class="rounded p-0.5 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"`
  - Target: `inline-flex h-11 w-11 items-center justify-center rounded text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground sm:h-8 sm:w-8`.
- `components/fleet/ApprovalBadge.vue` `data-testid="fleet-approval-notifications"` button
  - Baseline: `class="rounded-md p-2 text-muted-foreground hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground"`
  - Target: `inline-flex h-11 w-11 items-center justify-center rounded-md text-muted-foreground hover:bg-accent hover:text-foreground sm:h-9 sm:w-9`.
- `pages/settings/notifications.vue` checkboxes
  - Baseline: `#notification-email-master`, `notification-pref-<category>` and `notification-pref-email-<category>` use `h-4 w-4 accent-primary`; the in-app and email checkboxes sit in a `<span class="flex shrink-0 items-center gap-2 ...">`.
  - Target: all three use `h-5 w-5 accent-primary`. Each per-category `<span>` wrapper becomes a `<label>`
    whose `for` is the checkbox it holds and whose class adds `min-h-11 sm:min-h-0`, so the "In app" /
    "Email" text and the row height are part of the hit area. The in-app checkbox then has two labels with
    the same `for` (the existing category label and the new wrapper); that is valid HTML and its accessible
    name becomes the category text plus "In app". The email checkbox keeps its `aria-label`.
- `pages/[project]/flows/index.vue` state link
  - Baseline: `<NuxtLink :to="`/${slug}/flows/${flow.id}`">` with no class.
  - Target: the link carries `inline-flex min-h-11 items-center sm:min-h-0`.

**Scope** — In: the four named surfaces and their exact responsive class/label changes, preserving ids, data-testids, native actions, accessible attributes and notification setting semantics; four new behavioral test suites; and a negative-path regression assertion that the approval-notification toggle remains absent when browser notifications are unsupported. Out: US-001 breadcrumb links, US-002 disabled styling/reason wrappers, US-003 select/input sizing. Touch targets beyond the five R2-16 controls are not swept here. Measured touch-target sizes and contrast are checked in the post-merge live sweep on koda-wk, not in unit tests (jsdom has no layout). Do not alter audit permissions/detail logic, badge polling/streams/authorization, preference saves/rollback or flow paging.

**Interface** — Keep `audit-expand`, `fleet-approval-notifications`, `notification-email-master`, `notification-pref-<category>` and `notification-pref-email-<category>` identifiers. Each new category wrapper's `for` is the id of its enclosed checkbox. The flow state route remains `/${slug}/flows/${flow.id}`. No new component props, events or public TypeScript interfaces.

**Testing** — Use tdd-simple and create the four touch-target specs named in expectedFiles. Reuse mount harness patterns from tests/pages/admin-audit-detail.spec.ts, tests/components/fleet-approval-badge.spec.ts, tests/pages/notification-settings-page.spec.ts and tests/pages/fleet-flows-list.spec.ts. Mount an audit entry, supported browser notifications, a populated preference view and one flow. Assert class tokens and actual label parent/for relationships, with preserved email aria-label. Preserve the existing category label even though it shares the in-app checkbox's for. Use injected polling/live doubles, settle async mounts and unmount afterwards. Actual browser dimensions and contrast remain the post-merge live sweep, not unit assertions. No new request or error path.
acceptanceCriteria: Given one audit entry, when pages/admin/audit.vue mounts, the audit-expand button class includes h-11, w-11, sm:h-8 and sm:w-8.
Given browser notifications are supported, when ApprovalBadge mounts, the fleet-approval-notifications button class includes h-11, w-11, sm:h-9 and sm:w-9.

Given one category row, when pages/settings/notifications.vue mounts, notification-email-master, notification-pref-<category> and notification-pref-email-<category> each render with classes h-5 and w-5.

Given that notification-settings mount, when notification-pref-<category> renders, its parent is a label (not the existing category label, which shares the same for) whose for is notification-pref-<category> and whose class includes min-h-11 and sm:min-h-0.

Given that notification-settings mount, when notification-pref-email-<category> renders, its parent is a label whose for is notification-pref-email-<category> and whose class includes min-h-11, with the checkbox keeping its aria-label.
Given one flow record, when pages/[project]/flows/index.vue mounts, that row's state link to /<slug>/flows/<id> renders with classes inline-flex, min-h-11, items-center and sm:min-h-0.
Given browser notifications are unsupported, when ApprovalBadge mounts, no element with data-testid fleet-approval-notifications is rendered, preserving the existing unsupported-browser behavior.

routing.reasoning: Four existing UI surfaces receive deterministic class and semantic-label changes using current harnesses; no new state management, access checks or notification infrastructure.

analysis:
Refine-pass audit against .nax/features/web-shared-ui/spec.md:219-255: all 27 original acceptance criteria remain in their original stories and original order. Enumeration and mapping (spec number -> same story acceptanceCriteria position): US-001 #1 timeline/nav.timeline, #2 memory/nav.memory, #3 code-intel/nav.codeIntel, #4 settings/nav.settings, #5 approvals/nav.approvals, #6 approval-policies/nav.approvalPolicies, #7 existing flows and project-root arrays, #8 breadcrumb link classes plus a non-link leaf; US-002 #1 default muted disabled classes without opacity-50, #2 destructive muted disabled classes, #3 unchanged outline opacity-50 without muted background, #4 blocked Publish reason p/classes/wrapper/order, #5 matching button aria-describedby and reason id, #6 ask-mode/no-path enabled Publish without aria-describedby; US-003 #1 exact constant string, #2 real NativeSelect h-10/w-full/not h-9, #3 timeline select h-10/border-input, #4 both memory selects h-10, #5 outbox h-10/w-fit, #6 memory search h-10/border-input, #7 existing memory onChange -> applyFilters once; US-004 #1 audit responsive button classes, #2 supported-notification toggle classes, #3 all three checkbox sizes, #4 in-app parent label/for/mobile classes distinct from the existing category label, #5 email parent label/for/min-height with retained aria-label, #6 existing flow detail URL and responsive link classes. The i18n-stub qualification, both still-gives breadcrumb regressions, matching reason id, ask-mode Publish-enabled/no-reason parenthetical, before-and-after memory regression, existing category label sharing for, retained email aria-label, and flow destination qualification all survive. No deprecated grep/file/verbatim criteria occur in the spec. Composite rendered-output assertions from the spec remain intact rather than silently losing an element or qualifier. Each criterion is directly observable as a computed value, exported string, rendered tag/class/attribute/relationship or event emission/call count; pixel measurements are not inferred.

Negative-path and regression audit: US-001 #8 already checks an item without to renders a non-link span (AppBreadcrumb.vue:14-17), while #7 protects old route mappings. US-002 #4 checks blocked Publish, #6 checks absent aria-describedby when no reason exists, and #3 protects outline's old styling. US-003 originally lacked an explicit malformed/negative input case, so the refine request adds #8 preserving the already implemented null-target change fallback: update:modelValue emits the empty string (NativeSelect.vue:35-37). US-004 originally lacked an unavailable-control case, so the refine request adds #7 preserving absence of the toggle when browser notifications are unsupported (ApprovalBadge.vue:17). These two audit-added acceptance criteria are not claimed as original spec criteria and require no new error-handling logic, requests or workflows. US-003 #7 still proves native filtering survives the shared-class extraction; US-004 #4-5 retain existing label and accessible-name anchors. Descriptions explicitly include these unchanged-behavior tests without expanding the presentational implementation.

Context, routing and boundary audit: restored US-003's fifth contextFiles entry to the spec-recommended tests/pages/memory-readable.spec.ts instead of the less critical NativeSelect spec; the latter remains an explicit required read/test update in the implementation notes. All spec-listed context files now fit in the five-file limits (US-002 additionally includes the existing thread-handoff helper), and no story-created file is listed as context. Binding US-001 through US-004, apps/web workdirs and empty dependencies remain unchanged; no upstream output is needed. All four remain medium/tdd-simple: standard multi-file class/markup changes, no new integrations and no security-sensitive logic changes. Rechecked for description/AC contradictions: 40 px filter controls are distinct from the 44 px narrow-screen targets, disabled opacity overrides apply only to filled variants, the read-mode blocked Publish case is distinct from ask-mode no-path publishing, checkbox boxes are 20 px but their labels provide the mobile hit area, and unsupported-notification rendering remains conditional. All 10 expected new files (nine test files and lib/form-control.ts) match the spec's Creates list.

Out-of-scope audit: all seven feature-level items from spec.md:108-114 remain verbatim at top level: (1) deferred page-polish audit findings and separately open R2-21; (2) unchanged global breadcrumbs; (3) retained opacity-50 on outline/secondary/ghost/link; (4) unchanged unrelated raw selects with intentional FleetNativeSelect propagation; (5) no wider touch-target sweep; (6) no reason-layout changes outside ThreadActionBar; (7) post-merge live measurements rather than unit layout/contrast assertions. None was converted into an acceptance criterion. Nearby story Scope-Out text echoes the relevant exclusions, including the live-measurement boundary. No story-local deferral is hoisted, no fifth story or dependency is introduced, and test creation/helper extraction are expressly inside the corresponding story scopes.

Repository discovery: codebase-memory MCP tools are unavailable in this session, so investigation used direct Read, Grep and Glob tools rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. This is an enhancement to the existing web client, not greenfield work. The supplied Next.js detection is incorrect: apps/web/package.json:5-17 uses Nuxt commands and Jest/Playwright, and apps/web/package.json:36-40 declares Nuxt 4.6.4 and Vue 3.5.44. Follow .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:5-35: Nuxt 4 SSR, existing root-level pages/components/composables, Tailwind and local shadcn primitives. No backend, persistence, OpenAPI, generated client, new request, workflow or error-handling changes are needed. All four stories have workdir apps/web and dependencies []; they can be implemented independently. They are medium-complexity presentational changes using standard existing patterns and tdd-simple. Merely styling permission-bearing admin/approval screens does not change access control, credentials or sessions; retain every existing permission check and therefore do not introduce security-sensitive work into these stories.

Goal and completion: resolve audit findings R2-10, R2-12, R2-13 and R2-16, recorded at docs/ux/redesign/AUDIT-2026-11.md:56-62. Done means the six named project breadcrumb leaves, muted disabled filled variants, stacked accessible thread reasons, 40 px filter controls and specified mobile touch-target classes are implemented and their actual rendered output/path mapping matches each story's criteria. Unit tests assert semantic structure, class tokens and event wiring, not computed pixel size or contrast; post-merge verification on koda-wk must measure the 390 px targets and contrast in light/dark themes. There is no new failure mode to enumerate.

US-001 impact: apps/web/layouts/default.vue:105-188 computes breadcrumbItems, returns [] without project context, already distinguishes project root, threads, flows, labels, KB, fleet and ticket routes, but has no six requested branches. Reuse projectBase at line 115 so project ancestors link to /<project>; keep exact-path matching and all existing branches/fallback behavior. The layout renders AppBreadcrumb at apps/web/layouts/default.vue:444. apps/web/components/AppBreadcrumb.vue:1-19 accepts { label: string; to?: string } items and chooses NuxtLink for ancestors versus a span for the leaf; only link classes change. Existing translated nav keys are already present in apps/web/i18n/locales/en.json:66-97 and apps/web/i18n/locales/zh.json:66-97, so no locale additions are necessary. apps/web/tests/layouts/flows-nav.spec.ts:15-32 has breadcrumbItemsFor: compile the real layout setup, transpile import.meta, inject Vue/Nuxt globals and return breadcrumbItems.value; copy that harness into the new default-breadcrumb-leaves spec rather than testing a second mapping implementation. Its existing flows/root-adjacent regression assertions start at line 59. apps/web/tests/helpers/permission-nav.ts:82-90 provides globalPermissionsStub; apps/web/tests/helpers/fleet-harness.ts supplies i18nStub. Keep the inline sidebar template and its source ordering untouched: docs/ux/redesign/MASTER-PLAN.md:34-36 and .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:151-163 explain layout test pins. New component tests need an attribute-forwarding NuxtLink stub to inspect actual link classes and the unlinked leaf.

US-002 impact: apps/web/components/ui/button/Button.vue:1-40 composes a literal base, cva variantStyles and caller attrs through cn; disabled:opacity-50 appears both in the template base and the cva base. Add variant-level disabled:bg-muted disabled:text-muted-foreground disabled:opacity-100 only to default/destructive, leaving both bases and the remaining variants intact. apps/web/lib/utils.ts:1-6 implements cn as twMerge(clsx(inputs)); later disabled opacity classes replace earlier conflicts, so assert the final rendered button, not only the cva string.
